newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close sharply up on NCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close sharply up on NCD issue.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply higher on Friday as the central bank continued to issue T$3 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit to tighten banking system liquidity, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.427 percent against Thursday's 6.144 close, with 30-day commercial paper rising to 6.35-6.45 percent from 6.25-6.35.
The NCD issue was the seventh consecutive day of such intervention by the central bank.
The central bank's recent non-stop NCD issuance was seen widely in the market as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the sizzling stock market rally.
Taiwan's deputy central bank governor Liang Cheng-chin on Wednesday flatly denied that this was the case, saying the bank was acting purely in response to the liquidity situation.
Liang said banking system liquidity remained fairly loose, prompting the central bank to mop up excess funds.
On Friday, the stock index plunged 3.09 percent as an export ban on fresh and frozen pork and the government's latest attempt to cool down the overheated market triggered heavy selling.
The bond market did not report trade in the afternoon session. The 10-year 86/4 government bond yield was traded at 6.150 percent earlier against Thursday's 6.148 close.
